go_terms.name: positive regulation of voltage-gated potassium channel activity

description.text:
Drosophila QUIVER protein (qvr), also known as SLEEPLESS protein or SSS, is a small (~15kDa) glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI)-anchored protein from the Ly-6 family required for homoeostatic regulation of sleep under normal conditions and following sleep deprivation [[cite:PUB00075809]]. SSS is a novel potassium channel subunit that regulates the voltage-gated potassium channel Shaker (Sh) protein, a potassium channel which regulates the sleep [[cite:PUB00075810], [cite:PUB00075812]]. This interaction suppresses neuronal excitability and enables sleep [[cite:PUB00075812], [cite:PUB00075810]]. Besides the Sh modulation, SSS also antagonises nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) to reduce synaptic transmission and promote sleep [[cite:PUB00075811]].

This entry also includes paralogues of qvr called UPAR/Ly6 domain-containing proteins such as crim, rtv and bero from Drosophila melanogaster and the uncharacterised protein F46C5.4 from C.elegans.

PUB00075809.title: Identification of SLEEPLESS, a sleep-promoting factor.

PUB00075810.title: Drosophila QVR/SSS modulates the activation and C-type inactivation kinetics of Shaker K(+) channels.

PUB00075811.title: SLEEPLESS is a bifunctional regulator of excitability and cholinergic synaptic transmission.

PUB00075812.title: SLEEPLESS, a Ly-6/neurotoxin family member, regulates the levels, localization and activity of Shaker.
